p01.why: The constant evaluation calls through a null function pointer, which is undefined, and the Evidence says all compilers reject it.

p02.why: A class object with operator() can be called, and the constexpr call gives 8; there is no main.

p03.why: A member access to an earlier member inside the class being defined: GCC and EDG accept, Clang rejects because the class is incomplete (Q-0316).

p04.why: A function pointer does not point to an object type, so postfix ++ is not allowed.

p05.why: The call passes an argument for a parameter of incomplete class type Inc.

p06.why: An int is not a function, function pointer, or class object with operator(), so it cannot be called.

p07.why: A mutable member of a const object can be changed, and a reference member gives a non-const lvalue.

p08.why: Moving a pointer two past the end during constant evaluation: GCC accepts, Clang and EDG reject (Q-0031).

p09.why: The default argument fills b, and the ellipsis takes the extra arguments.

p10.why: The operand of -> must be a pointer to a class, and s is a class object.

p11.why: Postfix ++ and -- give the old value and change the operand by one, also for a pointer.

p12.why: The index of a built-in subscript must be an integer or unscoped enumeration, and 1.0 is a double.

p13.why: A pointer operand must point to a complete object type, and void is not one; -pedantic-errors turns off the GCC extension.

p14.why: The call gives one argument for two parameters with no default argument.

p15.why: Neither operand of the subscript is an array or a pointer.

p16.why: The operand of postfix ++ must not have enumeration type.

p17.why: The parameter is copy-initialized from 3.9, and the conversion drops the fraction, giving 3.

p18.why: W w(W()) declares a function w, so w.v applies . to something that is not a class object.

p19.why: A member call through a null pointer is undefined, and UBSan reports it on Clang and GCC and stops the run.

p20.why: A scoped enumeration is not allowed as a subscript index.

p21.why: The result of postfix ++ is a prvalue, so decltype((i++)) is int.

p22.why: Box has no operator() and no conversion to a function pointer.

p23.why: Member lookup does not find w in S.

p24.why: Inside the class definition the access sees only members declared before it, and later is declared after; Clang also rejects the incomplete class.

p25.why: The index is 4 for an array of 4, which reads outside the array; the UBSan bounds check stops the run.

p26.why: Decrementing the smallest int overflows, which constant evaluation rejects.

p27.why: The operand of postfix -- must not have type bool.

p28.why: A parenthesized member function access followed by a call is allowed, and a static member function reached by member access is an ordinary function, so auto gives a function pointer.

p29.why: The call's return type Inc is an incomplete class.

p30.why: The object expression get() is evaluated even for a static member, so calls is 1 and v is 5.

p31.why: n++ on the largest int overflows, and UBSan stops the run.

p33.why: Member lookup in Meter does not find scale; a free function is never found by member access.

p34.why: Handle has a conversion function to a function pointer, so h(4) is a call.

p35.why: An lvalue reference return gives an lvalue, an rvalue reference return gives an xvalue, and a value return gives a prvalue.

p36.why: The class Gauge is incomplete at the member access.

p37.why: Member lookup looks only in the class and its bases, so the global outside is not found.

p38.why: The call goes through a null function pointer; the run crashes and ASan reports the fault.

p39.why: A non-static member function reached by member access must be called.

p40.why: i++ on the largest int overflows during constant evaluation.

p41.why: The operand of postfix ++ must not be bool; Clang gives a pedantic diagnostic, which -pedantic-errors makes an error.

p42.why: a[2] reads outside the array during constant evaluation.

p43.why: A const int is not a modifiable lvalue.

p44.why: A pointer to int is not a pointer to a function.

p45.why: Parenthesized member accesses are called, member lookup finds Gauge::scale, and the explicit object member function is called with g as the object.

p46.why: x.f names a non-static member function and is not called.

p47.why: The call goes through a pointer of another function type: the Clang sanitizer stops it (run-fail), and GCC has no such check, so the run exits 0.

p48.why: A member of a prvalue is an xvalue, so decltype gives int&&.

p49.why: The operand of . must be a class object, and p is a pointer.

p50.why: cells[4] reads past the end of the new array, and ASan stops the run.

p51.why: Member access can name an enumerator, a static member, a member function call, a base member, and a qualified member; the specification does not cover the qualified forms, so this is a best guess.

p52.why: A member call through a null pointer during constant evaluation: Clang and GCC reject, EDG accepts (Q-0318).

p53.why: A subscript of an array member of a prvalue: Clang and GCC give int&& and accept, EDG gives int& and rejects (Q-0034).

p54.why: The member named by member access must not be a type.

p55.why: a[2] writes outside the array during constant evaluation.

p56.why: The call gives two arguments for one parameter and f has no ellipsis.

p57.why: ++ on a short at its largest value: Clang and GCC convert the value back to -32768 and accept, EDG rejects (Q-0124).

p58.why: obj.v, ptr->v, (*ptr).get(), and obj.s all give the expected values.

p59.why: S has a non-trivial copy constructor and goes through an ellipsis: GCC and EDG accept, Clang rejects.

p60.why: Unsigned values wrap around, and unsigned char steps in the promoted type then converts back to 0.

p61.why: &a[3] forms an address two past the end of a two-element array, which is undefined, so constant evaluation rejects it.

p62.why: a[1], *(a + 1), and 1[a] are the same, and a pointer can be subscripted.

p63.why: The pointer points to an incomplete class.

p64.why: i++ is a prvalue, so it is not a modifiable lvalue for the outer ++.

p65.why: s.f names a non-static member function and is not called.

p66.why: The parameter is copy-initialized, so the explicit constructor cannot convert 1 to S.

p67.why: An unscoped enumerator can be a subscript index.

p68.why: A subscript of an array lvalue is an lvalue, so decltype gives int&.
